Close a known money race in the Nxeon first-month-free promo. Work EXCLUSIVELY in /opt/nxeon-wt-promorace (branch feature/promo-race-fix). Do NOT touch other worktrees. node_modules symlinked. Do NOT run build/prisma commands — code only.

THE BUG (documented, low-severity but real): the first-month-free promo is granted at most once per account and once per IP (enforced by two DB unique constraints on `PromoRedemption` — see lib/promo-redemption.ts `claimFirstMonthFree`). Every order flow is atomic EXCEPT the VPS CARD path: it pre-screens eligibility (`firstMonthFreeEligible`), creates a Stripe checkout at the discounted price, and only claims the redemption at FULFILMENT (after the card clears), swallowing a lost claim. So a customer who submits TWO card checkouts concurrently — both before either redemption row lands — can get TWO discounted checkouts from ONE eligibility (two free months). Note: the promo is currently scoped to SHARED HOSTING only (firstMonthFreeAppliesTo), but the hosting order path is wallet-atomic; the residual race is specifically the up-front-settlement (card/Stripe) pattern. Fix it generally so it's airtight for any product the promo applies to.

STUDY FIRST: lib/promo-redemption.ts (claimFirstMonthFree, firstMonthFreeEligible, the PromoRedemption schema + its @@unique constraints, setPromoOrderRef, markPromoRenewed), lib/actions.ts payAndDeploy (the VPS card pre-screen + createOrderCheckout), lib/order.ts placeOrder (the atomic claim + charge-full-on-lost-claim), lib/stripe.ts createOrderCheckout, and lib/fulfil-checkout.ts (where the card settles and placeOrder runs with `sold`). Also how coupons solve the same problem for reference.

FIX APPROACH: RESERVE the redemption at checkout-CREATE time (before Stripe), and confirm/release it at fulfilment — so a second concurrent checkout can't also pass eligibility. The cleanest is to make the claim atomic at the moment of checkout creation (insert the PromoRedemption row with a PENDING/reserved state keyed to the Stripe session), then on fulfilment mark it consumed, and on checkout expiry/cancel release it (so an abandoned checkout doesn't permanently burn the customer's one eligibility). Reuse the existing unique constraints. Keep the invariant: at most ONE free month per account AND per IP, and never charge a customer MORE than displayed. If a reservation can't be made (already reserved/redeemed), re-quote the card leg at FULL price before checkout (mirrors the existing repeat-redeemer re-quote) so displayed===charged.

MONEY SAFETY (critical): no path grants two free months; no path charges more than shown; an abandoned/expired checkout must RELEASE the reservation (else a customer loses their offer to a checkout they never completed). Handle Stripe's async nature (webhook/confirm + expiry).

DELIVER end-to-end, then commit `git add -A && git commit -m "fix: reserve first-month-free across Stripe round-trip (close card-path double-claim race)"` (trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>), `git push -u origin feature/promo-race-fix`. REPORT (factual, detailed): files changed, schema changes (reservation state), exactly how reserve/confirm/release works across create→fulfil→expire, and how you proved no double-grant and no over-charge and no permanently-burned eligibility on abandonment. Don't claim tested.

content.thinking:
So the hosting setup uses wallet-atomic without Stripe checkout, meaning the only upfront card settlement happens through `createOrderCheckout` in the VPS path via `payAndDeploy`. The promo doesn't apply to VPS yet, but I need to fix the card payment flow to be robust for any product that might use it. I'm mapping out the sequence: `payAndDeploy` triggers `createOrderCheckout` to create a Stripe session, the customer completes payment, then `fulfilCheckoutSession` processes it and calls `placeOrder`.

The race condition is clear now—two concurrent `payAndDeploy` calls both see the customer as eligible, both create discounted Stripe sessions, both get paid, but only one wins the `claimFirstMonthFree` call at fulfilment time. On the card path, when a claim is lost, the code skips the fallback that would charge full price (because `sold` is already present), so the customer ends up charged the discounted amount without recording a redemption.

The fix is to reserve the redemption at checkout creation time, before Stripe, keyed to the session. Then at fulfilment, confirm the reservation. The same unique constraints on `promoId` and `userId` (or `ipHash`) prevent a second concurrent checkout from also reserving, forcing it to re-quote at full price instead.

I need to add a `state` field to `PromoRedemption` to track whether a redemption is reserved or consumed, defaulting to consumed so existing wallet flows maintain their atomic semantics.

I also need `sessionId` to link the reservation to the Stripe checkout session, and `reservedUntil` to track when an abandoned reservation should expire—Stripe sessions themselves expire after 24 hours by default, and we'll handle release through the cancel URL path.…

Committed and pushed. Here is the report.

## What was done

Closed the card/Stripe up-front-settlement double-claim race in the first-month-free promo by making the redemption a **reserve → confirm → release** lifecycle instead of a claim-at-fulfilment. Work is entirely in `/opt/nxeon-wt-promorace` on `feature/promo-race-fix` (pushed). No build/prisma commands were run.

### Files changed (8)
- **`prisma/schema.prisma`** — `PromoRedemption` gains three columns + one index (schema change below).
- **`lib/promo-redemption.ts`** — new `reserveFirstMonthFree`, `confirmReservation`, `releaseReservation`, `sweepExpiredReservations`, plus an internal `releaseExpiredReservationsFor` self-heal; `claimFirstMonthFree` now stamps `state: CONSUMED` and self-heals stale holds; `promoStats` counts `CONSUMED` only.
- **`lib/stripe.ts`** — `createOrderCheckout` takes `promoReservationToken`, sets `expires_at` (`ORDER_CHECKOUT_EXPIRES_MS = 1h`), stamps `nxeonPromoReservation`; `CheckoutPurpose.order` + `classifyCheckoutSession` parse the token.
- **`lib/actions.ts`** — `payAndDeploy` reserves the credit *before* opening checkout; on a lost reservation it re-quotes at full price and recomputes the split; releases the hold if the session fails to open.
- **`lib/order.ts`** — `placeOrder` card path confirms the reserved hold via the token instead of a fresh contended INSERT; wallet path unchanged.
- **`lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`** — forwards `order.promoReservationToken` into `placeOrder`.
- **`app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts`** — handles `checkout.session.expired` to release the hold.
- **`worker/index.ts`** — registers `sweepExpiredReservations()` on a ~2 min cadence.
- Added **`test/promo-race.test.ts`** (10 DB-free tests).

### Schema change (reservation state)
Added to `PromoRedemption`: `state String @default("CONSUMED")` (RESERVED | CONSUMED), `reservedUntil DateTime?`, `reservationToken String? @unique`, and `@@index([state, reservedUntil])`. The two existing `@@unique([promoId,userId])` / `@@unique([promoId,ipHash])` constraints are reused unchanged — a RESERVED hold occupies the same slot as a grant, which is what blocks a second claim. Default `CONSUMED` keeps every wallet-atomic flow (hosting/email/game/immediate-wallet-VPS) behaving identically with no code change. Deploy applies it via `prisma db push` (the repo has no migrations dir); the module accesses the new columns through the existing hand-typed `promoDelegate` cast, so it typechecks before the client is regenerated.

### How reserve/confirm/release works across create → fulfil → expire
- **Create (`payAndDeploy`)**: when `quote.promoCreditCents > 0`, insert a RESERVED row keyed by a generated token (`pmr_<uuid>`), with `reservedUntil = now + 1h + 10min grace`. The INSERT contends on the two unique constraints, so exactly one of N concurrent checkouts wins. Losers get `{reserved:false}` → re-quote full → recompute split → the stamped total and card leg are the full price. The token is stamped into the session metadata; the session's `expires_at` is 1h.
- **Fulfil (`fulfilCheckoutSession` → `placeOrder`)**: reads the token from metadata and calls `confirmReservation(tx, token)` inside the charge tx, flipping RESERVED→CONSUMED (guarded `state: RESERVED`, so idempotent under the redirect+webhook double-fire). The card already settled the discounted leg; confirm never issues a second debit. No token ⇒ order was sold full ⇒ nothing granted.
- **Expire/abandon**: `checkout.session.expired` webhook releases the hold by token (guarded to RESERVED); the worker `sweepExpiredReservations` deletes any RESERVED row past `reservedUntil` as a backstop if the webhook isn't configured; and both `reserveFirstMonthFree` and `claimFirstMonthFree` proactively delete the customer's *own* expired holds before contending, so the very next order attempt reclaims a stale hold immediately.

### Why the money invariants hold
- **No two free months**: the credit slot is held exclusively from *before* the first card is charged until confirm/release. A second concurrent create cannot insert its own hold (unique violation) and re-quotes full. The wallet path's atomic claim also collides with a live hold and charges full. `reservedUntil` is pinned *past* the session's payable window (grace), so a payment landing at the last instant still finds a live hold to confirm.
- **Never charged more than displayed**: the stamped `OrderPrice` and the card leg come from one quote; a lost reservation re-quotes full and recomputes the split *before* the session opens, so Stripe-page-displayed === settled. The confirm-null fallback keeps the already-paid discounted amount (never up-charges).
- **No permanently-burned eligibility on abandonment**: releases come from three independent sources (expiry webhook, worker sweep, and self-heal on the next claim/reserve), and release is guarded to `state: RESERVED` so a paid+confirmed grant is never revoked. Session lifetime is capped at 1h so recovery is prompt.

Note: the promo is currently scoped to HOSTING only and HOSTING is wallet-atomic, so for VPS today `promoCreditCents` is 0 and the reserve block is inert — the fix is dormant but correct the moment the owner extends the promo to any card-checkout product (per the "fix it generally" instruction). As a clean side effect, the card path no longer records a bogus redemption/`termPromoPercent=100` off `sold.promoPercent` (which `currentPromo` always stamps 100) for full-price VPS card orders.

- Full suite: **1077 pass** (1067 prior + 10 new), **6 fail**. I verified by `git stash` that those same 6 fail identically on the untouched base branch — they are pre-existing. Two of them (`checkout-metadata.test.ts:77` and `purchase-consent.test.ts:279`) are stale source-grep tripwires that already broke on earlier commits when `promoCampaign` and `{ipHash,campaign}` args were added to `createOrderCheckout`/`placeOrder`; my change adds one more arg so they stay red. The other 4 (fpm pool, `promoPriceCents` composition, term-rate recording, promo-bar catalogue) are unrelated to my files. I left them as-is to stay in scope.
- `tsc --noEmit`: **0 errors** project-wide.
- The 10 new tests are DB-free proofs (pure classifier + source tripwires) of the fix's shape: token round-trip, reserve-before-checkout ordering, full re-quote on loss, release-on-failed-open, card-path confirm (not fresh claim), fulfilment token forwarding, RESERVED-guarded release/sweep, expiry webhook, worker sweep. They do **not** exercise the concurrent claim against a live database — that would need a test DB, which I did not run.
